cards.text: The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, has a word about Moab, the nation that came from Lot's son Moab (Genesis 19:37). And friend, it does NOT open with "Hope you're doing well." It opens with woe to Nebo, a town in Moab, because it will be devastated.

cards.question: Next on the list is Kiriathaim, another town in Moab. The LORD says it will be captured and disgraced.

cards.text: And the praise Moab used to get? Gone. Over in Heshbon, people are plotting evil against her.

cards.question: The people in Heshbon are plotting evil against Moab. What do they say they'll do to her?

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to a town called Madmen. Friend, I didn't name it. I'm just reading it.

cards.question: The LORD says the people of Madmen will be silenced, and the ___ will pursue them.

cards.text: A voice cries out from Horonaim: "Devastation and great destruction!" Moab will be shattered, and her little ones will cry out.

cards.question: Moab's people are on the road, up the ascent to Luhith and down the descent to Horonaim. What are they doing as they go?
The cries of distress on the descent to Horonaim tell Moab to stand and fight.

cards.text: Nope. The cry is "Flee! Run for your lives! Become like a juniper in the desert." Then the LORD says why Moab will be captured.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say Moab will be captured?

answers.text: Moab trusts in its works and treasures
Moab attacked the city of Jerusalem
Moab broke its treaty with Egypt

cards.text: Trusting your works and treasures? Friend, I had sharp edges once, and soft edges are exactly how I ended up in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: It's not just the people. Chemosh, the god of the Moabites (1 Kings 11:33), will go into ___ with his priests and officials.
The LORD says a few of Moab's towns will escape the destroyer.
The LORD says, "Put salt on Moab, for she will be laid waste." What will her cities become?

answers.text: Desolate with no one living in them
Crowded with people running from war
Fortresses for the destroyer to keep

cards.text: Then comes a hard line: cursed is the one who is remiss in doing the work of the LORD.

cards.question: In that hard line about the work of the LORD, who else is called cursed?

answers.text: The one who holds back his sword from bloodshed
The one who takes the treasures of Moab
The one who mourns for the towns of Moab

cards.text: Now the LORD paints a picture. Moab has been at ease from youth, settled like wine on its dregs, never poured from vessel to vessel or gone into exile.

cards.question: Moab is like wine that never gets poured from vessel to vessel. What does the LORD say about his flavor and aroma?

cards.text: Years in one spot and nobody moves you? Friend, I did that in a junk drawer, and trust me, my flavor did NOT improve.

cards.question: The LORD says the days are coming when He will send wanderers to Moab. What will they do to him?

answers.text: Pour him out and shatter his jars
Seal his jars and guard them well
Fill his vessels up to the brim

cards.question: Once Moab is poured out like that, who will Moab be ashamed of?

cards.text: And the LORD gives a comparison: "just as the house of Israel was ashamed when they trusted in Bethel."

Then comes a question: "How can you say, 'We are warriors, mighty men ready for battle'?" That's me telling a baker I can lift a full cookie box with one mustache, five seconds before I'm on the floor UNDER the cookie box.

cards.question: The King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, says the best of Moab's young men will win the battle.
Moab's calamity is at hand, and his affliction is rushing ___.

cards.text: Next, the LORD speaks to all who surround Moab, everyone who knows his name.

cards.question: The LORD tells everyone around Moab to celebrate his fall.

cards.text: They're told to mourn for him and tell how the mighty scepter is shattered. Then the daughter dwelling in Dibon is told to come down from her glory and sit on parched ground.

cards.question: Why is the daughter dwelling in Dibon told to come down from her glory?

answers.text: The destroyer of Moab has come against her
She has turned away from the LORD her God
Her king has been taken away as a captive

cards.text: Over in Aroer, the people are told to stand by the road and watch. Ask the man fleeing or the woman escaping, "What has happened?"

cards.question: Moab is put to shame, for it has been shattered. Wail and cry out! Declare by the Arnon that Moab is ___.

cards.text: Then judgment comes on the high plain, town after town: Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath, Dibon and more, all the towns of Moab, far and near. Nebo and Kiriathaim, the first towns named back at the start, are on the list too.

cards.question: The LORD closes by saying Moab's arm is still strong.

cards.text: The horn of Moab has been cut off and his arm is broken, declares the LORD. That's where we'll leave Moab for now, friend, because the LORD's word about him isn't finished.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 15 quotes "Put salt on Moab, for she will be laid waste.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It repeats the answer to card 11 (trusting in works and treasures) and adds a joke, so it doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The core action of Jeremiah 48:7 is trusting in your own works and treasures. The comparison is about wearing down over time, which is a different action, so the joke doesn't click. It also implies Papa Dorin trusted in his sharp edges, which his backstory never says.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The joke adds something new to Papa Dorin's backstory: that he trusted in his sharp edges and that this is why he ended up in the drawer. The backstory only says he wore down and was replaced.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The question quotes 'she will be laid waste,' which almost states the right answer ('Desolate with no one living in them'). It also rules out the wrong answer 'Crowded with people running from war.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke reacting to 48:11, which cards 1 and 2 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke shows the boast collapsing ('five seconds before I'm on the floor UNDER the cookie box'). That gives away the answer to card 8, which asks whether Moab's best young men will win the battle.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Calamity is at hand' in the question rules out 'slowly,' which leaves only 'quietly' against the right answer. The card also just completes the verse's wording instead of testing meaning.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question includes 'put to shame,' 'shattered' and 'Wail and cry out!' These rule out both wrong answers ('restored' and 'victorious'), so the blank is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
